questions.text: I track my progress methodically to ensure I'm meeting my targets.
I work on whatever pulls me in, whether it's hard or easy, based on the moment.
I weigh the trade-offs of a decision on paper before committing.
I thrive when I have the trust of a group that works together.
I would skip my own vacation to cover for a coworker dealing with a family crisis.
I think about what tools or supplies I'll need before starting a project.
Someone else's suffering rarely makes me want anything at all for them.
I routinely document my own accomplishments so they are recognized and remembered.
I routinely set aside a portion of every paycheck specifically for helping others.
I experience the quiet moments of life — a still morning, a warm drink — with a gentle appreciation that never tips into intensity.
I offer feedback only when asked or when the group has a feedback culture in place.
When I understand that a person's pain is serious, that fact alone rarely makes me want to help.
I notice that major life events produce a proportionate, not outsized, emotional response in me.
When there is a vacuum of leadership, I look around to see who else might step in.
I do not usually detect when a question is rhetorical versus when someone actually wants an answer.
Someone's continuing hardship still matters to me long after I first heard about it.
I am concerned about what the people around me are going through.
I experience boredom not as a quiet absence but as an agitating restlessness.
I would use my professional influence to open doors for others rather than to advance my own agenda.
My inner emotional life is relatively smooth and consistent.
I pick up on when a person lingers after a group disperses because they want a private word with someone specific.
I am quick to declare a path forward when the group is circling.
Other people's problems only occasionally seem to matter to me.
I notice the way certain people in a group look to one specific person before reacting.
I notice when people adjust their vocabulary depending on who they are speaking to.
I do not naturally sense when a room is tense.
I am comfortable making commitments on behalf of my team without consulting them first.
I notice that strong emotions make me hyper-aware of my heartbeat, as if my body is broadcasting its state.
I rarely sense when a person is anchoring a negotiation through seemingly casual conversation.
I find budgets and financial plans too restrictive and prefer to manage money intuitively.
I tend to exit commitments that no longer align with where I want to go personally.
I tend to keep my most innovative ideas for my own ventures.
I like to try a different approach each time, even if the old way worked.
I often end up as the de facto leader in group projects.
I experience moments of tenderness with such intensity that they can bring me to tears.
When someone I love is in pain, I feel a strong wish to ease it.
